messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@hyperlane.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Tiered Dedicated Capacity — questionnaire attached

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for agreeing to participate in our RFP. Attached is Hyperlane's standard dedicated capacity questionnaire (dedicated_capacity_questionnaire_v2.xlsx). We're evaluating multiple vendors and need completed worksheets covering: GPU SKUs, steady-state throughput, expected tail latency (p95/p99), burst/peak behavior, and proposed reservation tiers (baseline, burst, fallback).

Key constraints:
- Production chat traffic: ~18k requests/day, target p95 token-latency <= 250ms for 2k-token context.
- Embeddings pipeline: 3M docs/month, batched at night with peak concurrency windows.
- Regulatory: all telemetry must remain in us-east-1; SOC2 evidence will be requested pre-contract.

Can you return the completed worksheet within 3 business days? Also include a short summary PDF if possible. If we need to schedule a short technical deep-dive for throughput mapping, suggest times next week (PST).

Regards,
Maya Shen
Procurement Manager, Hyperlane

Attachment: dedicated_capacity_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks — we've received the questionnaire and will prioritize it. I've looped in Ben (Solutions) and Karthik (Capacity planning) to complete the technical worksheet. We'll aim to return a filled workbook and a 1-page summary within 48 hours.

A couple quick clarifying questions before we complete numbers:
- For the chat p95 requirement, is the 2k-token context an average or a worst-case? Do you expect many concurrent long-context sessions or mostly short queries?
- For nightly embeddings, do you want a sizing target expressed as embeddings/second or total run-time (wall-clock) for a fixed batch size?
- For the fallback tier: do you want a cold start warmup (several minutes) for a lower-cost model or an active hot-standby that must meet identical latency?

Ben / Karthik — I'll capture your notes in redwood_scoping_notes_20260414.md and attach the workbook. Ben, can you include a conservative baseline and a quantized variant column? Karthik, please include assumptions about packing across GPU families (A10x / H100x / similar).

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP questionnaire — preliminary throughput draft

Lauren / team,

Quick draft numbers to seed the workbook. These are conservative and assume the model family Hyperlane mentioned (open-llm-13b-ish) with a transformer decoder profile. Notes below include assumptions; I'll add the full per-GPU worksheet cells to the spreadsheet.

Assumptions:
- Model: 13B dense / 8-bit quantized variant available.
- Target context for chat sizing: typical 400 tokens, worst-case 2k tokens for backtest.
- Safety margin: +20% for packing inefficiencies and KV cache warmups.

Per-GPU steady-state throughput (tokens/sec, single-request streaming):
- H100 80GB (mps-optimized): ~1,800 tokens/sec (single stream, 4 request batching efficiency)
- A800 / A10x class: ~650 tokens/sec (batched workload yields higher aggregate)
- 8-bit quantized H100 equivalent (mixed): ~2,700 tokens/sec (if model fully quantized and kernels available)

Latency p95 estimates (400-token chat):
- H100: ~110–160 ms
- A10x: ~240–320 ms
- Quantized H100 path: ~90–130 ms

Reservation tiers suggestion:
- Baseline (committed): sized to cover 70% of 30-day median throughput (steady-state), provisioned on H100-family nodes.
- Burst (on-demand reserved pool): additional credits to scale to 95th percentile traffic peaks, mix of A10x + burst H100 SKUs.
- Fallback (cost-optimized): quantized variants on dense A10x or single-tenant CPU fallback if tolerable; specify warmup plan.

Cost-sensitivity note: packing (concurrent streams per GPU) matters more for embeddings-heavy nights; we should size embeddings batch windows to maximize GPU utilization (bigger batches for A10x). For the RFP workbook I'll include throughput columns for: tokens/sec per-GPU, concurrent streams supported, reservation units, and suggested commit hours per month.

Questions for Hyperlane:
- Can you share a sample distribution of request sizes (tokens) and a representative week of traffic (UTC timestamps)? Even coarse percentiles let us map commit vs burst cost.
- Any hard SLA on p99? p95 is usually achievable but p99 requires dedicated tail capacity planning.

I'll populate the worksheet and send back the workbook and a 1-page summary by end of day tomorrow.

– Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP: Tiered Dedicated Capacity — questionnaire attached

Thanks, Ben / Lauren. Helpful prelims. A few clarifications from our side:

- Chat distribution: 60% of chats are short (<=80 tokens outgoing), 30% medium (80–600), 10% long (600–2000). We consider the 2k worst-case for analytics and fine-tuning; production steady-state is closer to 400 tokens.
- Embeddings: we typically measure as documents/hour; target is 3M docs/month with a daytime ingestion window where 80% of throughput happens across a 6-hour period (15:00–21:00 UTC).
- p99: not strict for chat tier but we expect p99 < 800ms for baseline SLA. If fallback tier is used, we need documented warmup strategy and explicit RTO (e.g., 5 minutes to hit 60% capacity).

For the fallback lane, please propose both: (A) a quantized hot standby that meets p95 but not p99, and (B) a cold-capacity plan that requires multi-minute warmups but is significantly lower cost.

We can share a coarse token-size histogram — attaching a redacted CSV. Also happy to schedule a 60-minute deep-dive on Thurs 16 Apr between 08:00–11:00 PST.

Thanks,
Aaron
Director, Platform Ops, Hyperlane

Attachment: hyperlane_token_histogram_redacted.csv

Aaron / Maya,

Thanks for the histogram and clarifications — that distribution helps a lot. Attached are three deliverables: (1) completed workbook (cells populated by SKU and suggested reservation units), (2) a short one-page summary, and (3) a draft SOW for initial scoping (draft_sow_hyperlane_dedicated_v1.docx). Key highlights below.

Executive summary (high level):
- Baseline commitment: sized to cover ~72% of median steady-state using H100-family nodes (estimated 12 H100 GPUs sustained, assuming 400-token average). This meets your p95 target comfortably and p99 under normal operating ranges.
- Burst pool: additional pool sized to handle 95th percentile peaks — recommended mix 8x A10x + 4x H100 on burst reservation to balance cost and warm-start time.
- Fallback lane: two options provided in workbook: hot quantized standby (meets p95, lower p99) and cold-on-demand lane (supports gradual ramp to 60% capacity within 5 minutes).

Action items / MAP:
- Week of Apr 19: Technical workshop (60m) to review packing assumptions and validate token histogram. Proposed slots: Thu Apr 16 08:30–09:30 PST (you suggested this window — confirm).
- Apr 21: We provide final numbers & a cost sketch with committed monthly fees and burst overage rates.
- Apr 23: Draft contract terms circulated (SLA language & SOC2 attestation attachments).

Requested from Hyperlane:
- Confirm whether the fallback lane must be hot-standby or if cold-warmup is acceptable for non-critical workloads.
- Share any specific compliance evidence requirements (IP allowlisting, KMS integrations, or audit log formats).

Next steps: I'll schedule the workshop and circulate a calendar invite once you confirm Thu morning works. Ben / Karthik / Priyom will be on the call for sizing and pricing Q&A.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
